title: Entity Model
description: A business concept in the semantic catalog — Security, Price, Party, File Load, Data Quality Exception. The entity is the unit of grounding: it is what a business user names, what the AI retrieves, and what a data source reads from. It deliberately carries no physical data reference.

domain.description: Grouping for navigation and retrieval. Open string: client deployments introduce domains we do not control.

primaryKey.description: Attributes identifying one instance. Used to build drill-down parameters automatically, so an author never wires key passing by hand.

labelAttribute.description: Attribute to display when this entity is referenced generically, e.g. in a tab title or a related-item list.

attributes.description: Object map keyed by attribute id, not an array — so JSON Patch paths into an attribute remain stable as the catalog grows.

effectiveDating.description: Whether instances are point-in-time, effective-dated, or bitemporal. Determines which of asOf and knownAs a data source may legitimately set.

logicalDataSourceId.description: Logical handle resolved to a physical target per tenant and environment by the Data Gateway. The presence of a logical id here, and the absence of any physical reference, is what makes an experience promotable between environments byte-identically.

rowEntitlementDomain.description: EDM entitlement domain governing which instances the caller may see. Resolved to row predicates by the Data Gateway at request time, from the caller's identity. Never resolved from anything in a page definition.

defaultDetailExperience.description: Experience to open when drilling into an instance of this entity. Declaring it once on the entity makes drill-down generic: any grid or chart bound to this entity can offer drill-down without the page author or the AI choosing a target, and every page drills to the same place.

cost.description: Coarse cost characteristics used by query planning, the design-time cost guard, and AI layout decisions (a high-cost entity should not be queried by twelve widgets on one page).

volatilityTtlSeconds.description: How long a result may be cached. A property of the data, known to the steward — which is why the gateway, not the client, decides cache TTL.

requiresFilter.description: True when an unfiltered query is never acceptable — a securities universe of millions of rows. Enforced by cost validation at design time.
